# general-simulator

> An open-source Rust simulator for piecewise-linear (PWL) circuits and mixed circuit/block-diagram systems. Resolves which segment every switching device is in as a Linear Complementarity Problem each timestep instead of Newton-Raphson + voltage limiting, and provides native control-theory blocks (transfer function, state-space, PID, discrete-time variants, coordinate transforms) so a digital control loop can be built directly in the netlist and validated against its own real, switching power stage.

## User Guide

For netlist authors: writing, running, and reading the output of a general-simulator netlist.

### The netlist and device-file grammar

- [Grammar overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/netlist-grammar.md): Your first netlist already showed the core convention: a kind=...
- [PWL devices: diodes and ideal switches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/pwl-devices.md): general-mna never stamps a real semiconductor's exponential I-V curve — no D-card model physics, no BSIM MOSFET.
- [Gate bindings (fixed, PWM, block-driven)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/gate-bindings.md): A note on this chapter's own title, before anything else: earlier project history (and this chapter's own outline) described several gate= variants — on/off, pwm, dutyctrl, dutyctrlcomplement, vco, block, vcophase.
- [Signals: `meas:`, `prev:`, and same-step references](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/signals.md): A note on this chapter's own title, before anything else: the skeleton this chapter was planned from was titled around meas:, prev:, and same-step references, as if meas: were a third, distinct signal kind alongside the

- [Sources and math operations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/sources-and-math.md): The Component Reference already has the full, authoritative field list for every block in this chapter (generated directly from the real doc comments, kept current automatically).
- [Dynamic blocks (PID, state-space, transfer function)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/dynamic-blocks.md): Every dynamic block in this chapter carries its own internal state across steps, unlike the stateless sources and math operations in Sources and math.
- [Coordinate transforms (Clarke/Park) and PLL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/coordinate-transforms.md): The six Clarke/Park transforms and the anglewrap PLL-angle utility turn a three-phase or rotating-frame control problem into something an ordinary kind=pid can regulate directly, instead of chasing a sine wave.
- [The PMSM block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/pmsm.md): kind=pmsm is a permanent-magnet synchronous motor in the rotor d/q frame — the standard textbook electromechanical model, built specifically to close the loop around the coordinate-transform blocks for a field-oriented-c
- [The CScript escape hatch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/cscript.md): kind=cscript loads a user-supplied, precompiled native shared library (.so/.dylib/.dll) and calls into it once per step.
- [The Python escape hatch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/python-blocks.md): kind=pyblock and kind=pyfunc embed a Python interpreter in-process (via PyO3) and call into a user-supplied .py file once per step — the Python-hosted counterpart to the CScript escape hatch, for reaching for numpy/scipy
- [The Octave escape hatch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/octave-blocks.md): kind=octfunc and kind=octblock call into a user-supplied, Octave-compatible .m file — the Octave-hosted counterpart to the Python escape hatch, for people with legacy .m-format scripts instead of Python.

- [`kind=measure`: ngspice/Xyce-style .measure statements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/measurements.md): kind=measure is a netlist line that computes one scalar (or, for four, a small handful of related scalars) from an already-completed transient trace — the same job ngspice's .measure and Xyce's .MEASURE statements do, ex

### Worked examples

- [Buck converter (open-loop and PID)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/examples/buck.md): A buck converter is the simplest place to see general-simulator's PWL/LCP approach and its block-graph controller layer working together: a hard-switched power stage (an kind=ideal_switch plus a freewheeling kind=ideal_d
- [Boost/LLC resonant converter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/examples/boost-llc.md): A boost converter uses the same Gate bindings PWM-driven pattern as the buck chapter — one actively-driven switch, one freewheeling diode, sum -> pid -> pwm if closed-loop — just with the inductor moved to the input side
- [Three-phase PFC active front end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/examples/pfc.md): A three-phase active-front-end power-factor-correction (PFC) rectifier exercises more of general-simulator at once than any other example in this guide: the Clarke/Park coordinate transforms, a synchronous-reference-fram
- [PMSM field-oriented-control drive](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/user-guide/src/examples/pmsm-drive.md): An id=0 field-oriented-control (FOC) speed loop driving a kind=pmsm block directly.

## Developer Guide

For contributors: the math, internal mechanism, and rationale behind every major design choice.

- [Introduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/introduction.md): This guide is for contributors, reviewers, and anyone who wants to trust the simulator enough to rely on its results for a real design decision.

### Architecture

- [Why not Newton-Raphson](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/architecture-overview.md): Every SPICE-family circuit simulator — ngspice, Xyce, HSPICE, and other commercial SPICE derivatives — solves a nonlinear DC or transient operating point the same way: Newton-Raphson on the KCL/KVL-plus-device-model syst
- [The generic Thevenin/LCP fold](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/lcp-formulation.md): This chapter is a walkthrough of crates/dae-runtime/src/lib.rs's own module-level doc comment (lines 1-25 as of this writing) — the real derivation already lives there, in the crate itself, as the authoritative source; t
- [DAE integration: backward Euler and trapezoidal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/dae-integration.md): Every circuit general-mna produces, and every continuous block this project supports (transfer function, state-space, PID, integrator — see docs/architecture.md's "One descriptor system for circuit and continuous blocks
- [Ringing detection and the backward-Euler fallback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/ringing-and-fallback.md): Trapezoidal integration is A-stable — bounded for any linear, stable mode regardless of step size — but it is not L-stable.

### Switching

- [Diodes and ideal-switch body diodes: the endogenous case](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/switch-model-diodes.md): lcp-formulation.md covers this in full; the short version needed here is that every segment of a diode's canonical decomposition shares one fixed reference conductance g_off, so switching segments only ever shifts an aff
- [Ideal-switch channel state: the exogenous case, and why](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/switch-model-ideal-switch.md): *This chapter is about pwl_devices::IdealSwitch — a PWL companion model (r_on when gated on, a PWL body diode when gated off), not real BSIM-style MOSFET physics.

### The block graph

- [Blocks as a descriptor-DAE fragment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/block-graph-descriptor.md): general-mna builds circuits as a single descriptor differential-algebraic system,
- [Computational causality: topological_order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/block-graph-causality.md): A block-diagram netlist can name its inputs in whatever order the author finds clearest — a Sum computing an error signal might read most naturally declared *before* the two sources that feed it.
- [Algebraic loop detection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/block-graph-cycles.md): A same-step cycle among Signal::Block edges — block A's input traces, however indirectly, back to A's own output in the *same* evaluation step — has no feedforward evaluation order that resolves it: whichever of the cycl
- [Dynamic blocks: one RK4 per block, wired by causality](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/block-graph-rk4.md): Every dynamic block — Pid, StateSpace, TransferFunction (via continuous_blocks::StateSpace:: rk4_step) and Pmsm (via its own bespoke step()) — integrates *independently*, once per circuit step, holding its own state in a

### Crate tour

- [Workspace layout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/crate-tour.md): The workspace (Cargo.toml, root of this repo) has eight members, built in a strict dependency order that was also the order they were *verified* in — that ordering is not incidental bookkeeping, it is how the project tru
- [`lcp-solver`: Lemke's algorithm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/crate-lcp-solver.md): The numerical primitive the whole project stands on: given M (n x n) and q (n), find w, z in R^n with
- [`pwl-devices`: ideal-diode and ideal-switch models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/crate-pwl-devices.md): Two device *curves*, and nothing else.
- [`dae-runtime`: circuit assembly and the transient loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/crate-dae-runtime.md): The crate where a netlist becomes numbers: it assembles a circuit's linear MNA system (built by general-mna, including its 'D' stamp) together with PWL device segments (from pwl-devices) into one Linear Complementarity P
- [`continuous-blocks`: the block library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/crate-continuous-blocks.md): The crate that turns block-diagram elements into numbers: transfer function, state-space, PID, voltage-controlled oscillator, hysteresis comparator, coordinate transforms, logic, and the stateless math ops.
- [`cscript-ffi`: the native escape hatch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/crate-cscript-ffi.md): Loads a user-supplied, precompiled shared library (.so/.dylib/.dll) and calls into it once per block instance per transient step — a dynamically-loaded, stateful escape hatch for block behavior no existing continuous-blo
- [`pyblock-ffi`: the Python escape hatch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/python-blocks.md): *(Implemented this session — this chapter records the design and the measurements that grounded it, mirroring vector-signals.md's own before/after structure.)*
- [`pyblock-ffi`: pure-function blocks (`kind=pyfunc`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/pyfunc-blocks.md): *(Implemented this session, as a genuinely separate, additive block kind alongside pyblock — not a mode of it.
- [`octave-ffi`: Octave blocks (`kind=octfunc`, `kind=octblock`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/octave-blocks.md): *(kind=octfunc implemented first, as a genuinely separate, additive block kind alongside pyfunc — the direct octave-cli-hosted analog, not a mode of anything else, mirroring pyfunc-blocks.md's own before/after structure.
- [`general-simulator-cli`: the netlist-in/CSV-out runner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/crate-general-simulator-cli.md): The general-simulator binary, and the thinnest crate in the workspace by design.
- [`kind=measure`: post-processing measurements, not a block-graph kind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/measurements-architecture.md): *(Implemented this session — this chapter records the architecture decision and the actual integration, mirroring python-blocks.md's own before/after structure.)*

- [Required gates and workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/workflow.md): The three commands every piece of work runs before it may be called done, verbatim from AGENTS.md's "Required gates" section:
- [Journal and gotchas conventions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/journal-and-gotchas.md): Two continuity mechanisms, both in docs/, both named in README.md's "Development" section as the things to consult before touching anything: "Continuity log: docs/journal/.
- [Project boundaries: the sibling repos](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLODI-Engineering/general-simulator/main/book/dev-guide/src/project-boundaries.md): This repo sits in a directory with several siblings, and which repo owns which piece of the system is a *rule*, not a convenience.
